title: GIRP note from F1: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The GIRP template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Goals
sections.html: Treatment-plan goals addressed this session include reducing panic symptoms (F41.0 Panic disorder) and managing catastrophic cognitions related to panic attacks through Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.

sections.title: Intervention
sections.html:
• Reviewed completed thought records from the past week.
  • Conducted in-session interoceptive exposure (spinning in chair for thirty seconds) to address somatic triggers of dizziness.
  • Utilized CBT scaling to rate anxiety levels during and after exposure.
  • Discussed medication updates (sertraline 50 mg) and conducted a routine safety check.

sections.title: Response
sections.html: Client reported a rough week with a panic attack at the grocery store on Tuesday, triggered by the thought of passing out in front of others (rated 90% in the moment, decreasing to 40% later at home). Client completed two of three assigned thought records. Client participated in interoceptive exposure; initial anxiety peaked at 6 and decreased to 3 within two minutes, recognizing that physiological sensations peak and pass. Client denied any thoughts of self-harm. Sleep was reported as poor (approximately four hours per night, waking at 3:00 AM). Client reported starting sertraline 50 mg two weeks ago with mild initial nausea that has since resolved.

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Complete thought records three times this week.
  • Practice the interoceptive spinning exercise once daily at home.
  • Visit the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and remain until anxiety decreases by half.
  • Attend individual therapy session next week at the scheduled time.
